stem.en: Kabir folds a chain with every oily bead buried and scores well. Then he swaps one buried oily bead for a plus bead and refolds. The score falls. What went wrong?

text.en: A charged bead buried among oily beads is high on the Hill: it has no water and no opposite charge near it. The chain refolds to bring it to the surface, and the old fold is lost.

feedback.en: Weight is not in the game. Charge is. A charge wants water or an opposite charge, and the oily middle has neither.
One charge in the middle of the oily core is enough to force a different fold. That is the next-but-one lesson, and a real disease.
The scoring is the pulls. Same chain, same fold, same score, every time.

explanation.en: Every bead has a place it sits lowest. Put a bead where it sits high and the whole chain pays for it. One swap can change the fold.
